prize_parts.citation: for the theory and first experimental realisation of circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of a superconducting artificial atom to a single microwave photon, and the dispersive readout it enables

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: circuit QED (B016) with Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf. After reading the full exchange I find the scientific case more secure, not less. The achievement is sharply defined: a 2004 theory proposal and two 2004 strong-coupling experiments showed that a single microwave photon in an on-chip resonator couples coherently to an engineered artificial atom, and the dispersive readout and resonator-mediated coupling that follow are measured, reproducible properties. Twenty years of independent replication settle maturity. Seven of eight members place it in their top four, and the three members who lead with it (Johansson, Mehlig, I) come from different subfields, while Johansson's field proximity is disclosed and I am discounting his enthusiasm accordingly. On the chair's first question, the 2025 prize honoured macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in a circuit, a property of one large degree of freedom. Circuit QED is a different physical result, light-matter coupling at the single-photon level in a solid-state system. A citation worded around strong coupling and dispersive readout, and not around quantum computing or superconducting circuits generally, keeps that line clear. On the trio, Blais as theory name with Wallraff and Schoelkopf as the two experimental groups is a clean split, and Mehlig's suggestion to keep the citation narrow is what lets the three names hold.
statement.case_against: The 2025 adjacency is a real exposure. A reader who sees two superconducting-circuit prizes in two years may conclude the committee is honouring the same community twice, and no wording removes that entirely. The credit boundary is also real: Girvin and Huang co-authored the founding 2004 proposal and the Yale group was larger than Schoelkopf alone. With a three-name limit I cannot include Girvin without removing Blais or one of the experimentalists, and I do not think that is better. Finally, optical lattice clocks (B031) have a two-name attribution that is, if anything, tighter, and their 10^-18 reproduction between independent laboratories is as mature as anything on the list; if the committee weighs the 2025 adjacency more heavily than I do, B031 is the better lead.

responses.point: Kroll leads with optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) for the clean two-name credit, independent reproduction near 10^-18 and the prospective redefinition of the second, and would rank circuit QED lower because of 2025.
responses.response: You have made the best case for B031 and I take it seriously: the attribution is tighter than mine and maturity is not in doubt. My difficulty is the one you name yourself. The 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize already honoured the precision-frequency lineage, and Lemonde, Lisdat, Takamoto, Ludlow and the ion-clock groups sit close to the credited pair. Against that, 2025 honoured macroscopic tunnelling, a different phenomenon from single-photon strong coupling. I would not make the redefinition of the second the reason to move now: the discovery stands without it. If the committee concludes that the 2025 adjacency is decisive, I would support B031, and I would want a citation limited to the lattice scheme and its accuracy.

responses.point: Lindroth leads with lattice clocks, judges the underlying atomic physics directly, and says the discovery, attribution and maturity line up with the fewest open questions, while flagging proximity to Wallraff's institution.
responses.response: Your technical judgement of polarisabilities and systematic shifts carries weight with me and I accept that the physics is demanding, not incremental. Where we differ is on lineage versus adjacency. You treat 2005 and 2012 as a reason to doubt the novelty of the clocks, and I treat 2025 as a smaller exposure for circuit QED because the phenomena differ. I am less certain than you that either exposure favours the clocks. On your ETH proximity to Wallraff, I do not think it is a conflict that requires you to withdraw, but I would ask you to say whether it changes your ranking of B016, since you place it as your first alternative.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first as a natural successor to 2025 and discloses that he directs a related centre at Chalmers, saying his support may warrant discounting or recusal.
responses.response: In round 1 I asked you for a technical argument on what the architecture adds beyond the 2025 phenomena, and your reply, the 2004 date, the dispersive readout and the bus, is what I needed; I use it in my own case. I still do not accept succession as a merit, and I would drop that framing from any citation. Your disclosure is clear. I propose that the committee record it and that your vote on B016 be given with that on record, while recognising that your technical knowledge of the 2004 history is also what lets us test the attribution. I would ask you to say whether Girvin's role is the one point on which your memory is uncertain, since you flag it.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the experimental Higgs discovery first, with Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee as founders and leaders, and favours founders over rotating spokespersons.
responses.response: I accept your argument that founders are a more defensible basis than spokespersons, and I withdraw my earlier idea of Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee. The difficulty remains that ATLAS and CMS each involved thousands of people, and a founder-based trio leaves out the physicists who analysed the 2012 data and the leaders who ran the collaborations at the discovery. I cannot show that the three names are uncontroversial, so I cannot make it the lead, though I accept that it is the clearest discovery in the strict sense.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first, accepts that the pairing mechanism is unresolved and Cao is not credited, but argues the central correlated-insulator result is already confirmed by many groups.
responses.response: I accept the distinction: the existence of the correlated insulators is reproduced widely, and only the pairing mechanism is open. My concern is attribution, not whether the physics is real. Without Yuan Cao, and with the parallel Dean, Young and Kim work, I cannot defend the trio as complete, and I would rather wait. You also say a committee that waits for a settled interpretation would put circuit QED ahead; I agree, and that is where I come out.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept that single-photon strong coupling is a distinct discovery from the 2025 macroscopic tunnelling, or will prefer a longer interval before another superconducting-circuit prize.
Whether Girvin and Huang must be recognised in some form; I cannot settle that from the supplied names.
Whether B031 would stand better than B016 if the 2025 adjacency is judged decisive; I regard the two as close.
Whether IceCube's source evidence will mature, as I think it will, and whether the credit can be limited to Halzen, Karle and Spiering.
statement.conflict_note: Documented connections: PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur and the KTH astroparticle group. I have no documented tie to circuit QED, Blais, Wallraff or Schoelkopf, nor to Katori or Ye. IceCube (B040) is in my own field and is now only an alternative; no collaboration is documented. Johansson's disclosed directorship of a related centre, Lindroth's ETH proximity to Wallraff and Olsson's Tokyo fellowship are noted for the record but are not mine.
